# TyraX game project - instructions for AI assistants

This is a **PlayStation 2 game generated by the TyraX editor**. The editor owns
the data model and regenerates the game's C++ from it on every build; the game
builds in Docker (PS2DEV toolchain) and runs in PCSX2.

## Rules that prevent lost work

1. **Never edit** files whose first line says `Generated by TyraX. Do not
   edit - regenerated on every build` (all `*.gen.cpp`/`*.gen.hpp`,
   `inc/scene_data.hpp`, `inc/terrain_config.hpp`, `Dockerfile`,
   `docker-compose.yml`, `Makefile`). Change the project data instead.
2. Files marked `Delete this line to take ownership` (`src/terrain_game.cpp`,
   `inc/terrain_game.hpp`, `inc/controls.hpp`, `inc/scripts/script.hpp`) are
   regenerated only while the marker is intact; delete the marker line before
   hand-editing them (they then stop receiving editor updates).
3. Game/scene data lives in `<name>.tyra` + `objects/<id>.json` (+
   `terrain-*.heights`), not in C++. `<name>.history` is disposable editor
   state. Assets live under `res/`.

## Where your code goes

- **Object scripts**: `src/scripts/*.cpp` (non-`.gen`), classes registered
  with `TYRA_OBJECT_SCRIPT(Name)`; API in `inc/scripts/script.hpp`. See
  `src/scripts/example_interaction.cpp`.
- **Custom flow nodes**: `flow-nodes/*.flownode` (header + `---` + C++ body;
  `call = fn` bodies live in `inc/scripts/flow_nodes.hpp`).
- **Custom screen effects**: `screen-effects/*.screenfx`.

## Flow graphs (game logic)

Every scene object owns a flow graph (in its `objects/<id>.json`), compiled to
`src/gen/flow_graph.gen.cpp` at build. Graph JSON:
`{"nodes":[{"id":1,"type":"OnStart","pos":[0,0],"str":"","num":[0,0,0,0]}],`
`"links":[{"from":1,"to":2,"kind":"exec"}]}` with link kinds
`exec`/`object`/`pos`/`bool`/`text`. Triggers have the exec output; actions
have only an exec input (wire each action from the trigger; Delay's "after"
output sequences over time). Object params resolve link → `str` name → self;
logic gates are pure and bridge back to exec via On Condition (rising edge).
Any text may contain `{{cross}}` (a pad-button glyph) or `{{action:jump}}` (the
glyph of whatever that action is bound to) - see docs/text-icons.md.
For buttons prefer the **On Action** trigger (`str` = an input-action name from
the project's Input Map, e.g. `jump` / `sprint`): it follows the current
binding, including a preset switch and the player's own in-game rebind.
`On Button` (raw pad button) and `On Key` (raw USB keyboard key) bypass that on
purpose - use them only for a fixed debug key.

## The TyraX editor CLI (use it - it validates)

The editor executable on this machine: `{TYRAX_EXE}`

- `--dump <projectDir>` - JSON summary (scenes, objects, every referencable name)
- `--list-nodes <projectDir>` - full flow-node catalog + JSON schema
- `--dump-graph <projectDir> <object> [scene]` - one object's graph
- `--apply-graph <projectDir> <object> <graph.json> [scene] [--append]` -
  validate + write a graph
- `--ai-graph <projectDir> <object> <prompt|file>` - AI graph generation
- `--refresh-gen <projectDir>` - regenerate game sources without building
  (fast codegen check; dangling references appear as `unknown ...` comments in
  `flow_graph.gen.cpp`)
- `--build <projectDir> [--run]` - full Docker build (+ PCSX2 launch)
- `--bake-gi <projectDir>` - bake global illumination + light probes
  (explicit; a build only reads the cache in `.res-baked/gi/`, so editing
  a scene falls its lighting back to classic shading until you re-bake)
- `--resave <projectDir>` - load + save with validation/migrations

## Building and debugging

Docker Desktop must be running for `--build`; output lands in
`bin/<name>.elf`. The running game's log is `bin/log.txt`; `TYRA_ASSERT`
failures print a block delimited by `======= TYRA =======` ...
`================` naming the file/line (a `Non-fatal` header = the game
recovered). Logs exist only in the debug build profile. Verify changes with
`--refresh-gen` + diff first, then `--build`.

## VS Code

The TyraX extension (`.flownode`/`.screenfx` highlighting + validation) is
recommended via `.vscode/extensions.json`; `.vscode/c_cpp_properties.json`
(PS2 include paths for IntelliSense) is regenerated by the editor.
